title: 생명 코드 연구소 NPC 마을 전경 추가 3장
design: Architecture and connected walking paths dominate; actual five village NPC identities retained; no large protagonist portraits.

scenes.title: 온실과 빵집 사이의 생활거리
scenes.camera: 24mm 거리 눈높이 · 남쪽 길에서 중앙 광장 방향
scenes.prompt:
Create ONE finished 16:9 landscape ENVIRONMENT ESTABLISHING image for the existing game Life Code Laboratory. This is an immersive village-walk cinematic keyframe, not a portrait, not a character poster, not a flat map, not a collage.
The first reference is the ACTUAL village map. Preserve its distinctive buildings as recognizable real walkable places: round cream central laboratory with teal glass dome and brass ring magnifier; NW cream mushroom cottage with teal curved roof; NE teal-roofed pond observation house on timber piles with round glass turret; E archive with giant open-book roof ornament; SE cream bakery with brick dome oven, cream canopy and wheat patch; SW timber glass greenhouse. Keep deep teal roofs, cream stone walls, gold-tan curving lanes, railings, gardens and forest streams. Do not invent a new European city, castle, towers or extra main facilities.
IMPORTANT COMPOSITION: Buildings, roads, water and environmental depth occupy over 90 percent of the image. The camera walks THROUGH a full-size village: big near architectural edges, a human-scale street in the middle, the next recognizable destination farther away. Strong near/middle/far layers and curved leading lines. Do not spread every building around a central toy island. No aerial overview that simply copies the whole map. Do not center any character or have any character facing/posing for the viewer.
NPCs are small everyday inhabitants embedded in the environment, maximum 8 percent of the IMAGE HEIGHT each, 15–30 meters from the camera, with natural mundane tasks. No large foreground character, no character close-up, no staged group pose, no giant chibi head. Each mammal has precisely two arms and two legs, each bird precisely two wings and two feet, paws hold props simply, no extra or merged limbs. Reference character appearances are exact and species must not change.
Premium warm storybook animation environment with tactile painted stone, wood, ivy and lively but coherent cinematic depth, matching the supplied map's colors. Soft warm morning/late morning light. Healthy forest and ordinary village life, no disaster or magical ecosystem resurrection. No text, letters, signs with writing, UI, labels, captions, logo, watermark or speech bubbles. Preserve a calm lower foreground for optional subtitles without adding a blank strip.
SCENE 1 — WALKING THE SOUTH VILLAGE STREET.
Camera about 1.3 meters above the lane, 24mm environmental wide lens. We stand on the curving southern village road, looking toward the central observatory, which is a SMALL destination in the middle distance, not dominating the whole image. At extreme LEFT foreground a cropped greenhouse porch, chunky timber post and glass wall create a large architectural frame; its flowering planter and wood stair occupy the near left corner. Across the lane on RIGHT is the bakery's recognizable cream facade and teal roof, wide cream canvas canopy, brick dome oven and fenced wheat/herb garden. These street-facing buildings feel close enough to enter. The tan lane bends between their doors and continues clearly to the distant central circular plaza and dome; its path must remain open, with little garden gates and connected steps.
Reference 2 is BORI, the small honey-brown bear fermentation artisan wearing white shirt, indigo apron and yellow neckerchief. Place Bori far enough away to be TINY, about 6–8 percent of image height, at the bakery's outdoor counter right middle distance, arranging two small loaves in a basket using just two paws. Reference 3 is BAMTOL, the small hedgehog gardener with brown spines, cream shirt and orange apron. Bamtol is equally small beside the garden fence, carrying one leaf basket with two paws. Let their two simple activities imply the lane's daily rhythm. Do not make them a foreground pair.
Add ordinary lived-in environmental details: stacked empty crates under the canopy, oven tools on a wall hook, a watering can by the greenhouse, slightly worn paving at doorsteps, small curtains and flowers. No other animals or humans, no Moa/Toto portraits. The foreground lane is empty so the viewer can imagine stepping forward. No grand vista of every facility; this is a convincing walk between actual buildings.
scenes.videoPrompt: Use the attached image as the exact first frame. One continuous 8-second 16:9 environmental shot. Make a slow eye-level forward dolly along the existing empty tan street toward the distant central dome, as if the learner were walking. The near greenhouse porch and bakery canopy pass with clear, gentle parallax; buildings stay anchored and doorways remain connected to the street. Bori makes one small bread-arranging movement with its two paws at the bakery counter; Bamtol takes two small steps beside the garden holding its basket with two paws. Keep both NPCs small, naturally occupied and away from the lens. Maintain the exact two arms and two legs for each mammal, species and clothing unchanged. Do not move the camera toward a character or create a portrait. Preserve the calm lower path. No new buildings, duplicate NPCs, extra limbs, text, subtitles, UI, voices or music. Silent footage, 24fps, warm storybook lighting.

SCENE 2 — THE POND BOARDWALK AND THE NORTH FOREST LANE.
Camera at 1.1 meters above a waterside timber boardwalk, 28mm environmental wide view. Strong leading boardwalk railing runs diagonally from the LOWER RIGHT foreground into the middle distance. The recognizable pond observation house is the LARGE nearby building on the RIGHT half: cream walls, teal roof, small round glass turret, timber stilts anchored in turquoise pond water, wraparound timber balcony, accessible front stairs. Crop a little of its near roof/eaves to feel physically close, rather than fitting the whole object as a model. Lily pads, clear water, reeds and stepping rocks fill the LOWER LEFT foreground; a real connected small stone bridge and tan curved path lead away left toward the mushroom specimen cottage nestled in forest in the MIDDLE LEFT DISTANCE. Glimpse a partial central teal dome through intervening trees, not a full town panorama. All paths and stairs visibly connect and are walkable, no people standing in water.
Reference 2 is YEOUL, the friendly brown otter water keeper in a sage/teal field shirt holding a closed sample jar. Yeoul is TINY, at most 8 percent of image height, standing safely on the observation house balcony at middle right, setting a closed jar on a small display shelf with exactly two forepaws. Reference 3 is SOLBI, the orange squirrel specimen keeper with big fluffy tail, cream shirt, olive vest and specimen tray. Solbi is SMALLER again near the distant mushroom cottage gate, carrying the tray along the path with two paws.
This is an active inhabited research neighborhood: a small plain drying rack on the deck, neatly placed clean jars, a coiled rope, flower planters on the railing, ripples and a curtain slightly open. No open water-sample dumping, magical microbes or unsafe postures. No dominant portrait, no characters near the camera. Camera composition should make the viewer want to follow the rail and bridge to the next building.
scenes.videoPrompt: Use the attached image as the exact first frame. One continuous 8-second 16:9 wide environmental shot. Glide gently along the right-hand boardwalk toward the observation-house stairs, at walking speed, with strong near railing parallax and the distant stone bridge staying stable. Water has small ripples and reeds move lightly. Yeoul places its existing closed jar on the existing shelf using just its two forepaws, then pauses; the jar remains closed. Far away, Solbi takes two small steps on the existing path with its tray held in its two paws. Preserve both species, clothing, body proportions and two arms throughout. Keep architecture dominant and NPCs small; no zoom toward faces. All deck supports, stairs, railings and connecting paths stay geometrically stable, no people walking on water. No new objects, organisms, text, UI, subtitles, voices or music. Silent footage, 24fps.

SCENE 3 — TURNING THE ARCHIVE CORNER INTO THE VILLAGE PLAZA.
A cinematic 24mm wide view from underneath the eastern archive cottage's porch roof, standing just beyond its doorstep and looking diagonally west/southwest toward the circular plaza. The VERY NEAR RIGHT third is the archive's cream stone wall, substantial wood porch column, a few shallow entry steps, external book cabinet and partly cropped recognizable OPEN-BOOK ornament along the teal roof/eave. This close architecture should create a real street corner and a sense of shelter above the viewer. At lower LEFT foreground a curved low stone garden wall and bench guide our eye into a tan lane that curls LEFTWARD into the broad circular plaza. The central round laboratory's teal dome and brass roof ring are in the MIDGROUND LEFT of center, large enough to recognize but not centered symmetrically. Across the plaza behind it, only a glimpse of the glass greenhouse is visible; along the lower curving lane, a glimpse of the bakery canopy on the far left. Respect the existing game's small forest campus, not a city of added houses. Make clear several exits so we can mentally choose where to walk next.
Reference 2 is DURI, the small brown owl archivist wearing little round gold spectacles, cream shirt and dark waistcoat, carrying a red-brown closed book under one wing. Duri is TINY, maximum 8 percent of image height, just outside the archive doorway right midground; other wing relaxed down. Reference 3 is BORI, honey-brown bear in indigo apron and yellow neckerchief, carrying a bread basket in its two paws on the curving lane, also TINY. Reference 4 is BAMTOL, hedgehog gardener in orange apron, small and farther away tending the plaza flowerbed with a leaf basket on the ground. They are three separate everyday activities, not posing or staring at the camera.
A sunlit lived-in square: small wooden delivery crate beside the book cabinet, a broom resting against the archive wall, flower planters, scuffed entry stones, dappled foliage. Keep foreground path unoccupied and visibly leading into the plaza. No new people, no large characters, no ceremonial card presentation, no identical symmetrical postcard view. Warm daylight consistent with the preceding street and pond images.

Begin under the archive porch and slowly round the existing corner toward the central plaza, a short forward-left dolly with a subtle left pan. The near wood column and book cabinet move past the frame edge, revealing a little more of the existing curved lane and distant observatory. Duri takes one short step out of the archive holding its book under one wing, other wing relaxed; Bori takes two small steps along the lane with its bread basket; Bamtol makes one small gardening movement by the flowerbed. Keep NPCs small and dispersed, never a posed group. Preserve owl's two wings and two feet and mammals' exactly two arms and two legs. Architecture stays fixed; no teleportation, newly invented streets, large character closeups, text, UI, subtitles, speech or music. Silent footage, 24fps.
